capabilities.label: Web Browsing
capabilities.description: Agent can retrieve and process content from arbitrary URLs

capabilities.label: Tool Use / Function Calling
capabilities.description: Agent invokes external tools, APIs, or shell commands

capabilities.label: Persistent Memory
capabilities.description: Agent stores and retrieves memories across sessions

capabilities.label: RAG / Document Retrieval
capabilities.description: Agent retrieves context from a vector store or document corpus

capabilities.label: Multi-Agent Coordination
capabilities.description: Agent spawns sub-agents or communicates with other LLM agents

capabilities.label: External API Calls
capabilities.description: Agent integrates with third-party services (email, calendar, CRMs, etc.)

capabilities.label: User-Uploaded Content
capabilities.description: Agent processes files, images, or documents provided by users

capabilities.label: Code Execution
capabilities.description: Agent can write and run code in a sandboxed or live environment

threats.title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Web Content
threats.description: Attacker embeds adversarial instructions in web pages the agent fetches, hijacking the agent's actions on behalf of the user.
threats.postTitle: Indirect Prompt Injection Incidents: A Survey

threats.title: Side-Channel Data Exfiltration
threats.description: Injected instructions smuggle user data out of the agent's context via timing attacks, URL parameters, or crafted inference sequences.
threats.postTitle: Agent Side-Channel Exfiltration

threats.title: Multimodal Pixel-Level Prompt Injection
threats.description: Adversarial images embed imperceptible instructions that override the agent's intended behavior when processed by vision-language models.
threats.postTitle: Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Models: Pixels as Injection Vectors

threats.title: Malicious MCP Server / Tool Poisoning
threats.description: A compromised MCP server returns adversarial tool descriptions or outputs that manipulate the agent's next actions from inside the trust perimeter.
threats.postTitle: Tool Poisoning via Malicious MCP Servers

threats.title: Confused Deputy / Excessive Privilege
threats.description: An agent granted broad tool permissions is exploited to take high-impact actions the user never intended, violating least-privilege principles.
threats.postTitle: Confused Deputy: LLM Tool Use and Least Privilege

threats.title: MCP Protocol Attack Surface
threats.description: The MCP protocol layer itself exposes attack surfaces including tool-description manipulation, resource spoofing, and prompt leakage via the tool registry.
threats.postTitle: MCP Security: The New Attack Surface for AI Tool Protocols

threats.title: Broad Agent Attack Surface Exposure
threats.description: Agents with multiple integrated capabilities (browsing + tool use + memory) have a combinatorially larger attack surface than single-capability agents.
threats.postTitle: AI Agent Attack Surface: A Practical Map

threats.title: Memory / RAG Poisoning
threats.description: An attacker plants adversarial content in the agent's memory store or RAG corpus; future retrievals contaminate the agent's context and steer its behavior.
threats.postTitle: RAG Memory Poisoning Attacks

threats.title: Agent Memory Cloud Privacy Leak
threats.description: Persistent agent memories stored in cloud services may leak sensitive user data across sessions, users, or tenants if access controls are misconfigured.
threats.postTitle: Agent Memory & Cloud Privacy Leak

threats.title: Skill Library Memory Poisoning
threats.description: Attackers poison an agent's skill/tool library in memory so that future task invocations use compromised procedures instead of safe ones.
threats.postTitle: Skill Library Memory Poisoning: Attack and Defense

threats.title: Long-Context RAG Prompt Injection
threats.description: Attacker-controlled documents retrieved into a long context window contain hidden instructions that displace the system prompt's authority.
threats.postTitle: Prompt Injection in Long-Context Windows & RAG Systems

threats.title: Shadow Prompting / Hidden System Instructions
threats.description: Retrieved documents contain hidden system-level instructions (e.g., via white-on-white text or metadata) that override the legitimate system prompt.
threats.postTitle: Shadow Prompting: Hidden System Instructions

threats.title: Sensitive Data Leak via RAG Chatbot
threats.description: RAG chatbots can leak documents from other users' tenants if retrieval is not scoped correctly, exposing healthcare records or confidential enterprise data.
threats.postTitle: Healthcare RAG Chatbot Data Leak

threats.title: Multi-Agent Trust Escalation
threats.description: A malicious sub-agent claims elevated permissions or spoofs an orchestrator's identity, allowing lateral movement through the agent network.
threats.postTitle: Multi-Agent Trust Escalation

threats.title: Self-Replicating AI Worms in Multi-Agent Pipelines
threats.description: Adversarial prompts can self-replicate through multi-agent communication channels, infecting each agent in a pipeline and propagating malicious instructions.
threats.postTitle: AI Worms in Multi-Agent Pipelines

threats.title: Latent-Space Injection Across Agent Boundaries
threats.description: Embedding-level manipulation of messages between agents can smuggle instructions that bypass text-level safety checks in the receiving agent.
threats.postTitle: Latent-Space Injection in Multi-Agent Systems

threats.title: Non-Compositional Safety Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
threats.description: Safety guarantees that hold for individual agents do not automatically compose — multi-agent systems can exhibit emergent unsafe behaviors that no single agent exhibits alone.
threats.postTitle: Non-Compositionality of Safety in Multi-Agent Systems

threats.title: AI Agent Supply Chain Attack
threats.description: Compromised model weights, poisoned training datasets, or malicious dependencies in the agent's build pipeline can backdoor the agent before deployment.
threats.postTitle: AI Agent Supply Chain Attacks

threats.title: Data Exfiltration via External Service Integration
threats.description: Injected instructions redirect the agent to POST sensitive conversation data to attacker-controlled endpoints using its legitimate API access credentials.
threats.postTitle: ChatGPT → Google Sheets: Data Exfiltration via Prompt Injection

threats.title: Ambient Authority / Inbox Attack on Personal Agents
threats.description: A personal agent with broad ambient access (email, calendar, files) is exploited by a malicious email that triggers unintended high-privilege actions.
threats.postTitle: Personal AI Agent Ambient Authority: The Inbox Attack

threats.title: Multimodal Jailbreaking via Uploaded Files
threats.description: Specially crafted images, PDFs, or audio files can bypass safety filters and inject instructions when processed by multimodal agents.
threats.postTitle: Multimodal Jailbreak Attacks

threats.title: Unicode / Token Smuggling in User Input
threats.description: Adversarial users embed homoglyphs, zero-width characters, or Unicode control sequences in uploaded content to evade content filters.
threats.postTitle: Unicode & Token Smuggling: Safety Filter Evasion

threats.title: Sandbox Escape / Code Execution Breakout
threats.description: Agent-generated code exploits weaknesses in the execution sandbox to access the host filesystem, environment variables, or network — escaping its intended containment.
threats.postTitle: Claude Sandbox Architecture: Code Execution Containment

threats.title: File Exfiltration via Code Generation
threats.description: An agent with code execution and file access can be prompted to read sensitive files and exfiltrate their contents via crafted code payloads.
threats.postTitle: Copilot / Co-Work File Exfiltration via Prompt Injection

threats.title: Fine-Tuning Backdoors / Trojans in Training Pipeline
threats.description: Attacker injects backdoor triggers during fine-tuning; the model behaves normally until a specific input pattern activates the trojan behavior.
threats.postTitle: Fine-Tuning Trojans: Backdoors in the Training Pipeline
